explanation: Fires on subword pieces in the middle of rare proper names, place names, scientific or technical terms (e.g. 'A[[vey]]ron', 'B[[ör]]nert', 'P[[omer]]ania', '-apple[[-m]]acosx'). It also fires on scattered function words in lists of named things ('such[[ as]]', 'Bush and[[ Bill]]'). There is no single clear context beyond rare or foreign-name fragments.

Fires on a mixture of tokens that show no common theme. These include license boilerplate in code headers ('subject[[ to]] the terms', 'compliance with the[[ License]]'), hash or encoded fragments, file paths, and suffixes of biomedical words ('hepar[[in]]', 'pup[[ae]]').

Fires strongly on the return-type keyword 'void' in method or function declarations in Java, C#, C++ and Objective-C, especially after 'public static', 'private' or '- ('. Outside code it is weak to absent; only occasional weak hits on other code identifiers.

Fires on the '(' right after a news dateline city at the start of a wire story, before the agency name (e.g. 'TEHRAN, Iran[[ (]]AP)', 'LONDON[[ (]]Reuters)'). It fires more weakly on the comma after a dateline city ('TORONTO[[,]]'). It responds moderately to other formulaic document openings, such as patent 'The present invention relates' and court-case headers.

Fires most strongly on Russian (Cyrillic) words in programming Q&A or informal text, often the first word of a clause ('[[В]] customizer.php', 'нужно чтобы[[ по]]'). It responds moderately to idiomatic or discourse words in informal English ('the[[ same]] goes for', 'for the life[[ of]] me', 'that's[[ right]]').

Fires on a mixture with no common theme: Java/Kotlin import package segments ('org[[.jetbrains]]', 'java.awt[[.Color]]'), Japanese katakana at the start of a word, brand or proper-name completions ('Fiat[[ Chrysler]]', 'Colin[[ Kaepernick]]'), the word 'links' in 'External links', and suffixes such as 'gran[[ule]]' and '-less'.

Fires on a diffuse mixture of code tokens ('stack[[.append]]', 'return dy[[dt]]', 'Import-[[Module]]') and ordinary prose words and word pieces. No consistent feature of the token or its context stands out.

Fires on keywords that open a nested block or scope in code: a subquery 'SELECT' after '(', 'namespace' (especially nested namespaces), and 'function' in '(function' callbacks or inner functions. It also fires on 'class', 'type', 'def' and 'template' when they start an indented inner declaration. It is weak on 'the following' in license text and absent in plain prose.

Fires on separator punctuation inside compact multi-part identifiers: the '.' in version numbers ('1.0[[.]]0', 'php5.4[[.]]3'), and hyphens, slashes or colons joining parts of compound names, dates, times or citation IDs ('Arg-Gly[[-]]Asp', 'top/left[[/b]]ottom', '08:32[[:]]57'). It is weaker on initials and commas in name lists.

Fires on a mixture of tokens: the 'duct' piece of 'reductase' or 'reductant', the opening quote of a JS module path after 'from', names of software products ('MS[[ Word]]', 'in[[ Access]]', 'gnup[[lot]]'), and other pieces of technical or named terms. There is no single shared feature.

Fires on a mixture of tokens. The main groups are closing XML/HTML tags '</' (indented end tags), the word 'links' in the wiki heading 'External links', and electronics or semiconductor terms ('PM'OS, 'IG'BT, 'wire' bonding, 'photodi'ode).

Fires on the first piece of a word that has been split into several tokens, mostly in non-English (Portuguese, Spanish, Norwegian, Danish) text or on foreign proper names ('[[ Gian]]luigi', 'S.C.[[ Be]]ira-Mar', '[[ b]]arks'). It also fires on short function words like 'de' and 'og' in those languages. In plain English common words it is weak.

Fires on fragments inside rare proper names and Latin species names, often right after an initial or capital letter ('Crataegus[[ la]]evigata', 'X.[[ la]]evis', 'Gregory[[ Up]]church', 'C[[un]]ha'). It also fires on the '.A' in the legal citation 'U.S.C.A.'. The token has to be in the middle of an unpredictable name.

Fires on the comma, or a word like 'These', 'which' or 'including', at the point where a general category noun is about to be followed by examples or a list ('various types of information[[,]] such as', 'a variety of cells[[,]] including', '[[ These]] included'). It also fires on category nouns such as 'traits' and 'forms' in that position.
